name: The Deadpan Hotline
why_it_works: Absurd questions answered with a completely straight face create comedy from contrast, and each straight answer smuggles in a real fact or policy. Because the questions are clearly invented ('calls we haven't gotten yet'), nobody feels mocked, and the viewer leaves knowing exactly how to reach you.

hook.pattern: Frame it as calls the front desk hasn't gotten yet, then answer the first ridiculous one immediately.
examples: Calls our front desk is ready for. Just in case.
Questions nobody has asked {{brand}}. Yet. We have answers.
Our receptionist rehearses for these calls. Nobody has made them.

variables.name: absurd_question_1
variables.description: First invented question: odd but harmless (8 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: Can you fix a car that's just sad?

variables.name: real_answer_1
variables.description: Straight answer that slips in a real fact (8 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: Yes. Full diagnostic in 30 minutes. Sadness included.

variables.name: absurd_question_2
variables.description: Second invented question: sillier (8 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: Can my car wait in the lobby?

variables.name: real_answer_2
variables.description: Straight answer with a second real fact (8 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: You get the coffee. It gets bay 2.

variables.name: absurd_question_3
variables.description: Third invented question: the biggest (8 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: Can you make my minivan look fast?

variables.name: real_answer_3
variables.description: Straight answer that pivots to the main offer (8 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: No. But it can pass inspection today.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer can book, with its article, no end punctuation

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, copied from the matching pack in compliance/packs.json

beats.on_screen_text: Calls we haven't gotten yet. We're ready.
beats.voiceover: Calls we haven't gotten yet. We're ready.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 medium shot of a receptionist at the {{brand}} front desk wearing a headset, perfectly composed, hands folded, neutral face, clean bright reception light, centered
Vertical close-up of the {{brand}} receptionist speaking into the headset with total seriousness, a phone-call caption bubble area at top of frame, soft office light
Vertical shot from behind the {{brand}} receptionist toward the lobby, the receptionist calmly pointing at the waiting area while on the call, inviting warm light, everyday details

beats.purpose: peak and turn: question three pivots to the offer

visual.prompt: Vertical clip, the {{brand}} receptionist hears the question, blinks once, slowly takes a sip of coffee, then answers without any expression, slow push-in, steady office light
Vertical medium shot of the {{brand}} receptionist pressing the headset button, already looking at the next line, one eyebrow slightly raised, same framing as the opening shot

cta: Call with a real question, or book {{offer}}. Weird ones welcome.

craft.technique: Deadpan straight-man with escalating absurd inputs
craft.notes: Setup: the premise that these calls haven't happened, so the absurdity is the brand's imagination, not a customer's. Escalation: three questions climb from odd to silly to ridiculous while the answers stay flat and useful; the receptionist never reacts more than a blink. Turn: on question three the answer is a flat 'No.' followed by the real offer, which flips the joke into the pitch. Tag: 'Next caller.' returning to the opening framing, which implies there are more and invites comments. Timing: answer questions one and two with zero pause so the deadpan feels practiced; on question three hold the blink and coffee sip for about one second before the 'No.' That held sip is where the laugh lives.

do_not: Use questions that real customers actually asked; that turns the joke into mocking them
Let the receptionist smirk, laugh or roll their eyes
Put a fact in an answer that isn't true for this business today
compliance: Chiropractor: no answer may claim to cure, treat or fix a named condition; keep answers to scheduling, process and comfort
Insurance: no answer may promise coverage, a price or a claim result; add 'coverage varies by policy and state' to the caption
Mortgage: no rate, approval or payment promises in any answer; show NMLS ID and Equal Housing Opportunity in the caption or end card
Use the business's real staff or a clearly fictional actor, never a lookalike of a real person
